walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 3: Composition — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 3: Composition brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 3: Composition.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1725 Gradus ad Parnassum codified species counterpoint?
options: Fux
Rameau
Tartini
Albrechtsberger

mcqs.q: Which famous four-note motif begins Beethoven's Fifth?
options: Short-short-short-long
Long-short-short
Long-long-short-short
Short-long-long-short
Rapid alternation between the written note and the note a step above.
Three notes played at once.
Vibrato on a single note.
It has only five notes.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
All notes are raised by a semitone.
Three notes played at once.
It has only five notes.

mcqs.q: What does modulation mean in music?
options: Changing tempo or dynamics.
Three notes played at once.
Changing from one key to another within a piece.
Adjusting volume electronically.
